statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Cross-asset pressure is unusually aligned, but persistent one-way NQ structure is not independently verified.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold; the highest conditional risk is concentrated around the 14:30–16:30 Berlin data-and-cash-open window.
headline: Cross-asset pressure keeps Nasdaq Tail risk at the top of WATCH
body: Long-end U.S. yields are near multi-decade stress levels, Brent is around $91, global equity futures and Asian markets are weaker, and Strait of Hormuz disruption has intensified. Fresh delayed Finviz context also shows softer NQ, firmer VIX futures and weak megacap breadth. Because that feed is contextual and fresh independent NQ bar structure is unavailable, Tail remains 24% rather than crossing the block threshold.

lookbackSummary: Over the prior 24 clock hours, Tail rose from the high-teens into WATCH while Stress climbed from 90% to 98%. The latest two published hours were WATCH at 24% Tail as oil, long yields and geopolitical risk became more aligned.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours center on the 14:30–16:30 Berlin U.S. data-and-cash-open sequence. Forecast Tail stays at or below 24% because future one-way structure is not assumed. Risk can fall quickly if retracements are normal and cross-assets stabilize; FOMC minutes remain a high-impact calendar item for Wednesday.

forecast.analysis: Current cross-asset evidence is risk-off: delayed NQ is about 0.7% lower, S&P e-minis are softer, long yields and oil are elevated, and VIX futures are firmer. Persistent NQ bar-level extension is not independently verified, keeping Tail at 24% WATCH.

If elevated oil, long yields and volatility persist into the European morning, directional pressure remains plausible; without verified repeated NQ extension or failed retracements, Tail stays capped at 24%.

European price discovery is expected to test whether the overnight risk-off mix broadens. A two-sided NQ response or stabilizing yields would argue against escalation; persistent alignment would keep WATCH pressure elevated.

Absent new escalation, the pre-U.S. session should allow some stress decay. Tail can ease if NQ shows meaningful retracement and cross-assets stop extending; renewed oil/yield pressure would challenge that path.
Midday Europe is a lower-event-density hour. The key conditional test is whether NQ remains orderly while markets absorb high oil and long-end yields; no future one-way continuation is assumed.

Approaching the U.S. data cluster, event sensitivity rises again. Tail remains at the top of WATCH because housing/import-price releases are near, but event proximity alone does not establish mean-reversion failure.

The 14:30 Berlin housing and import/export-price releases create a concentrated price-discovery checkpoint. Tail remains conditional at 24%; escalation requires actual sustained extension and weak retracement after the data.

Industrial production at 15:15 Berlin and the approaching cash open compress multiple catalysts into one hour. Risk is high, but the forecast does not presume a directional outcome before it is observed.

The 15:30 cash open and 16:00 pending-home-sales release can amplify any existing move. Tail remains 24% unless opening structure shows persistent extension, shallow pullbacks and aligned cross-assets.

The first post-open hour remains sensitive to delayed second-leg behavior. If price discovery becomes two-sided and volatility stabilizes, Tail should recede; persistent extension would invalidate that normalization path.
With the scheduled data sequence largely absorbed, conditional Tail eases if retracements appear and cross-asset pressure stops widening. Residual oil and yield risk keeps Stress elevated.

Later U.S. morning trading shifts emphasis from event shock to path quality. Mean-reverting swings would reduce Tail further; repeated extensions after failed pullbacks would be the main adverse condition.
Early U.S. afternoon has fewer scheduled catalysts. Conditional risk declines if breadth and megacaps stop aligning directionally and NQ trades away from session extremes.

Mid-afternoon risk remains headline-sensitive because Hormuz conditions are unresolved. Without a fresh geopolitical discontinuity or persistent NQ trend, Tail stays in WATCH rather than block territory.
The U.S. power-hour approach can revive directional liquidity effects. Tail is conditional at 20%; a stable, two-sided session would support further normalization into the close.
Power-hour trading remains a checkpoint for late-session continuation versus reversal. No continuation is assumed; Tail stays modest unless NQ repeatedly extends and closes near an extreme.

After the cash close, scheduled equity catalysts are limited. Tail falls to the low band if the session ends without a persistent no-retracement path, though geopolitical headline Stress remains high.

Early evening futures trading should be calmer if the cash close is orderly. Any fresh Hormuz escalation or renewed long-yield surge would raise Stress first and Tail only if price-path persistence follows.
Overnight Asian handoff is modeled with low Tail but still-high Stress. Conditional risk depends on whether global equities and rates stabilize rather than extending the prior risk-off alignment.
During the early Asia session, two-sided index trading and stable oil would support low Tail. A renewed cross-asset selloff would lift conditional risk, but is not treated as already observed.
Later Asia hours remain primarily a cross-asset confirmation window. Tail stays low unless NQ, yields, volatility and regional equities align into persistent directional efficiency.
Approaching the European handoff, conditional risk remains low if overnight ranges hold and retracements are normal. Geopolitical headlines remain the main discontinuity channel.
Early European pre-open conditions can reprice overnight macro and oil developments. Tail remains low unless fresh evidence shows sustained NQ extension with confirming yields and volatility.

By the next European morning, attention starts shifting toward Wednesday's FOMC minutes later in the day. Tail remains low in this hour because the minutes are not yet imminent and no future reaction is assumed.
